newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CRICKET-AUSTRALIA THRASH WEST INDIES BY 124 RUNS.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-AUSTRALIA THRASH WEST INDIES BY 124 RUNS.

text.p: Australia thrashed West Indies by 124 runs in the second cricket test on Tuesday after wrist spinner Shane Warne produced his best bowling spell since returning to the test arena.
West Indies, who lost the first test in Brisbane by 123 runs, were dismissed for 215 in their second innings after surrendering their last five wickets for 39 runs before tea.
Warne, whose long-term effectiveness as a strike bowler was questioned after finger surgery in May, claimed four for 95 to help his side take a two-nil lead in the five-test series.
But it was the nature of the dismissals that will have particularly pleased Australia captain Mark Taylor.
West Indies opener Robert Samuels and number five Shivnarine Chanderpaul were bowled by balls that spun a prodigious distance off the wicket as both batsmen attempted mis-judged cut shots.
Warne later mesmerised West Indies wicketkeeper Courtney Browne with a succession of deliveries that beat the bat before he removed tail-enders Kenneth Benjamin and Courtney Walsh.
Warne bowled with menace throughout the innings, turning the ball more sharply than he did on his return to test cricket in Brisbane.
Chasing a victory target of 340, West Indies' hopes tumbled early in the day when they slumped to 35 for three.
But there was controversy surrounding the dismissal of number three batsman Brian Lara, his side's most influential player and a potential match-winner.
Lara, the world record holder for the highest score in test and first-class cricket, fell for one when he edged a catch to wicketkeeper Ian Healy.
Television replays raised doubt as to whether the ball carried and umpire David Shepherd delayed his decision for several seconds to consult with his colleague Darrell Hair.
Chanderpaul delayed Australia for almost three hours, adopting a positive attitude in scoring 71 before he was bowled by Warne with the final ball before lunch.
